notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input in ledgerly/invoice.py by raising BillingError(code, detail) with snake_case codes such as "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount"; reuse the same code for the same condition across functions (e.g. issue_invoice also uses "invalid_state").
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Coerce amounts with to_money and ZERO: Wrap raw Decimal amounts with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total do, so arithmetic stays consistent across the money module.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0004] Reject bools when validating integer quantities: When validating integer fields like quantity, explicitly exclude bool via isinstance(quantity, bool) before the int check, since True/False are ints in Python.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
